title: Rational exponents
goal: I can work with exponents that are fractions.
teach: a1/n = ⁿ√a and am/n = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. Take the root first so the numbers stay small. A negative rational exponent also means “one over”.
watch: The denominator of the exponent is the root; the numerator is the power.

qs.hint: A power of ⅓ means the cube root.
qs.steps:
1. Law (rational exponents): am/n = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. Take the n-th root first, then raise to the power m.
2. 8⅓ = ∛8
3. = 2, because 2³ = 8

qs.hint: The bottom of the exponent is the root; the top is the power.
qs.steps:
1. Law (rational exponents): am/n = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. Take the n-th root first, then raise to the power m.
2. 27⅔ = (∛27)²
3. ∛27 = 3, so 3² = 9

qs.hint: The bottom of the exponent is the root; the top is the power.
qs.steps:
1. Law (rational exponents): am/n = (ⁿ√a)ᵐ. Take the n-th root first, then raise to the power m.
2. 16¾ = (⁴√16)³
3. ⁴√16 = 2, because 2⁴ = 16
4. 2³ = 8
